text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over months or years, and many people have few or no noticeable signs in the early stages.

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar pulls fluid out of your tissues, making you feel thirstier than usual and leading to more frequent bathroom visits, especially at night.
Persistent fatigue: When your cells cannot properly absorb glucose (sugar) from your blood to use for energy, you can feel unusually tired or run-down.
Blurred vision: Excess sugar in the blood can cause fluid to shift into the lenses of your eyes, leading to temporary swelling and blurry sight.
Slow-healing cuts or sores: High blood sugar damages blood vessels and impairs circulation, slowing down your body's natural healing process.
Frequent infections: Elevated glucose levels can weaken the immune system, leading to more frequent skin, gum, or urinary tract infections.
Tingling or numbness: Peripheral nerve damage (neuropathy) from chronic high blood sugar often starts as a prickling, numbness, or burning sensation in the hands or feet.
Darkened skin patches: A condition called acanthosis nigricans causes dark, velvety skin folds—most commonly around the neck, armpits, or groin—and is a visual sign of insulin resistance.
Unexplained weight changes: While some people experience sudden weight loss because the body starts burning muscle and fat for energy, others may experience weight gain or increased hunger.

text_blocks.snippet: If you notice any of these symptoms or have risk factors like a family history or age over 45, a healthcare provider can check your blood sugar using standard diagnostic tests detailed by the Cleveland Clinic:

list.snippet: Fasting plasma glucose test: Measures blood sugar after an 8-hour fast (126 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes).
A1C test: Measures average blood sugar levels over the past 2 to 3 months (6.5% or higher indicates diabetes).
Random plasma glucose test: Measures blood sugar at any time without fasting (200 mg/dL or higher with symptoms indicates diabetes).
